what: The compute_uwshcu_inv surrogate (340 k-parameter MLP with the packed subset block, uwshcu_h256_notr_2cap_sub.pt) timed offline on one A100 against one CPU thread of the same node, at the hook's granularity (16 columns a call, arrays in host memory, the packed output back in host memory) and in larger batches of real columns; float64 in and out, the arrays Fortran-ordered as the hook hands them.  Not a model run: an offline measurement of what batching columns across ranks could give a GPU.
supersedes: the 2026-09-17 record (job 7513230), whose batches above 1,600 columns were capped by the number of captured calls it stacked (the tool sliced a shorter stack to the labelled size), so its rows for 4,096 and 16,384 columns timed 1,600 columns; the tool now refuses a batch larger than its source
node: one Derecho GPU node (main queue, select=1:ncpus=8:ngpus=1:gpu_type=a100)
inputs_from: the compute_uwshcu_inv anchor dataset: the first 16,384 of 200,000 real columns captured from the model (tools/extract_pi_cam_anchor_columns.py), every batch a distinct set of columns
in_image_reference: FTorch on the CPU nodes, 128 ranks a node sharing memory bandwidth: 4.17 ms a call live over the month (7510379)
conclusion: At one chunk a call the A100 is slower than one CPU thread (1.01 ms with the copies, 0.60 ms resident, against 0.61 ms): the call is launch-latency bound.  With the copies the GPU costs 6.4 us a column at 256 and about 3 us from 1,024 upwards (2.9 us at 16,384), against 17 us for the CPU thread at 256 and 42 us at 4,096 (the strided Fortran arrays stop fitting its caches); so a batched call pays from a few hundred columns, and its cost is the host-to-device traffic of the twenty input arrays, not the arithmetic (resident, 16,384 columns take 3.3 ms).  The hook never has that many columns a call; the batching plugin (validation/pi_cam_pausable_g35-uwshcu-sub-*-gpu-batch*) measures what gathering a GPU's 32 ranks gives inside the model.
